penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: Diagnosing and resolving a specific SSIS/Salesforce Bulk API stall at 800k rows requires deep hands-on investigation per customer — log analysis, connector config review, environment-specific debugging. This cannot be automated by Claude for each case.

penalties_applied.name: high_touch_support
penalties_applied.reason: Enterprise data engineers will have follow-up questions, edge cases, and escalations that require expert human judgment for each engagement.

rationale: The pain is real and production-critical — enterprise data teams running Salesforce ETL pipelines are clearly paying buyers (they already spend $1k–5k/year on KingswaySoft). However, the solution is inherently a consulting/professional-services engagement: each customer has a unique environment (SSIS version, SF org config, row volumes, network conditions) requiring bespoke diagnosis. Neither delivery nor support can be meaningfully automated, making this incompatible with the autonomy-first factory model. The penalties reflecting per-customer manual work bring this well below the validate threshold.
solution_plan: Not recommended for build. This would be a diagnostic advisory service for Salesforce bulk-load failures. While the buyer is real and paying, solving their specific pipeline stall requires hands-on access to their environment, logs, and configurations — work a human expert must do per-engagement. A solo non-technical operator relying on Claude cannot realistically diagnose and fix production ETL failures at the required depth. This is a consulting play, not an autonomous micro-service.
notes: Fails operational_autonomy (4 < floor of 7) and buildability_with_ai (4 < floor of 6). Per-customer manual work disqualifies this for the factory model. Drop.
